data.long_meaning: Derived from the Roman name 'Marcus', meaning 'Mars' (the god of war) + 'cellus' (little). Hence, 'Young Mars'. In Christianity, St. Marcellinus was a third-century bishop and martyr in Carthage. The name Marcellinus carries the meaning “Young Mars” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew, Greek. Parents who choose Marcellinus usually hope their child will grow to embody young mars and live with faith, good character and purpose.

in_latin.long_meaning: Marcellinus, meaning 'little Marcus,' is a Latin name that originated from the Roman gens Marcellus. The name is derived from the Latin words 'Marcus' and the diminutive suffix '-ellinus.' In Christian tradition, the name Marcellinus is associated with several early Christian martyrs, including Saint Marcellinus, a 3rd-century martyr who was beheaded in Rome during the reign of Emperor Diocletian. The name Marcellinus is also found in the writings of early Christian authors, such as Eusebius and Jerome.

in_english.name: Marcellinus

in_english.long_meaning: Marcellinus, a name with deep roots in Latin and Christian tradition, is derived from the name Marcus, meaning 'warlike' or 'dedicated to Mars.' The diminutive suffix -ellinus adds a youthful or diminutive form to the name, signifying a smaller or younger form of Marcus. In biblical context, the name Marcellinus is not directly mentioned, but it is associated with several early Christian martyrs, including Saint Marcellinus, who was martyred during the reign of Emperor Diocletian. The name Marcellinus is also found in the writings of early Christian authors, such as Eusebius and Jerome, who revered the name for its spiritual significance and cultural importance.

data.spiritual_significance: The name Marcellinus carries the spiritual meaning of a brave warrior for God. data.spiritual_symbolism: Marcellinus: Dedicated to Mars, the Roman god of war, symbolizing courage and strength in the Christian context. Spiritually, it represents a warrior of faith, steadfast in the battle against spiritual adversities.

historical_references.reference: Marcellinus was a bishop of Ancona, Italy, during the early Christian period. He is best known for his role in the trial and execution of the heretic Priscillian, which took place between 380 and 385 AD.
historical_references.context: The trial of Priscillian and his followers was a significant event in the early Christian Church as it established the power of the bishops in dealing with heretics and set a precedent for the Inquisition in the Middle Ages.

historical_references.reference: Marcellinus was also a pope, serving from 308 to 309 AD, during the period of the Roman persecutions of Christians. He is known for his courage in refusing to renounce his faith and was martyred during the persecutions.
historical_references.context: The Roman persecutions of Christians were a series of edicts and campaigns aimed at suppressing the Christian faith. Many Christians were executed for their refusal to renounce their faith, and Marcellinus is one of the many martyrs from this period.
